-- calls Luau turns into FASTCALL or folds when the arguments are constants: math, bit32, string
-- and buffer, with arguments at their edges, and the same builtins through locals and upvalues
print(math.floor(-2.5), math.ceil(-2.5), math.abs(-0), math.max(1, 5, 3), math.min(-1, -5), math.sign(-3))
print(math.floor(2 ^ 31 + 0.5), math.fmod(-7, 3), math.fmod(7, -3), math.clamp(15, 0, 10), math.round(-2.5))
print(bit32.band(0xff, -1), bit32.bor(1, 2, 4), bit32.bxor(5, 3), bit32.bnot(0), bit32.lshift(1, 31))
print(bit32.rshift(-1, 28), bit32.arshift(-16, 2), bit32.extract(0xabcd, 4, 8), bit32.replace(0, 7, 4, 3))
print(bit32.countlz(1), bit32.countrz(8), bit32.lrotate(1, 33), bit32.btest(6, 1), bit32.byteswap(0x01020304))
print(string.byte("ABC", 1, -1), string.char(72, 105), ("x"):rep(3, "-"), ("Hello"):sub(-3), ("Hi"):len())
print(("%5.2f|%-4d|%x|%s"):format(3.14159, 7, 255, "s"), ("a,b,,c"):split(",")[3] == "", #("a,b,,c"):split(","))
print(("hello world"):gsub("o", "0"), ("abc"):gsub("%w", "%0%0"), ("x=1 y=2"):gsub("(%w)=(%w)", "%2=%1"))
print(("key=val"):match("(%w+)=(%w+)"), ("  trim  "):match("^%s*(.-)%s*$"), ("a1b2"):find("%d"))
print(tonumber("0x10"), tonumber("10", 2), tonumber(" 5 "), tonumber("5e2"), tonumber("abc"), tonumber("z", 36))
print(type(nil), typeof(1), select("#", 1, nil, nil), select(-1, "a", "b"), rawlen({ 1, 2, 3 }), rawlen("abcd"))

local buf = buffer.create(16)
buffer.writeu8(buf, 0, 255)
buffer.writei16(buf, 1, -2)
buffer.writef32(buf, 4, 1.5)
buffer.writestring(buf, 8, "rosetta")
print(buffer.readu8(buf, 0), buffer.readi8(buf, 0), buffer.readi16(buf, 1), buffer.readu16(buf, 1))
print(buffer.readf32(buf, 4), buffer.readstring(buf, 8, 7), buffer.len(buf), buffer.tostring(buf):byte(9))

-- the same builtins through locals and upvalues, which compile differently
local floor, band, sub = math.floor, bit32.band, string.sub
local function viaUpvalues(v)
	return floor(v), band(v, 3), sub("abcdef", v, v + 1)
end
print(viaUpvalues(2), viaUpvalues(5))

-- a global that shadows a builtin library stops it being treated as one
local saved = math
local function sneaky()
	local math = { floor = function()
		return "shadowed"
	end }
	return math.floor(1.5)
end
print(sneaky(), saved.floor(1.5))

local t = { 3, 1, 2 }
table.sort(t, function(x, y)
	return x > y
end)
table.insert(t, 1, 0)
print(table.concat(t, ","), table.remove(t), table.find(t, 3), #table.create(3, "x"), table.unpack({ 1, 2, 3 }, 2))

-- A tokenizer and recursive-descent parser for arithmetic, with variables and errors.

local function tokenize(source)
	local tokens = {}
	local i = 1
	while i <= #source do
		local c = source:sub(i, i)
		if c:match("%s") then
			i += 1
		elseif c:match("%d") then
			local number = source:match("^%d+%.?%d*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "number", value = tonumber(number) })
			i += #number
		elseif c:match("[%a_]") then
			local name = source:match("^[%a_][%w_]*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "name", value = name })
			i += #name
		elseif c:match("[%+%-%*/%^%(%)=]") then
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = c })
			i += 1
		else
			error(`unexpected character '{c}' at {i}`, 0)
		end
	end
	table.insert(tokens, { kind = "end" })
	return tokens
end

local Parser = {}
Parser.__index = Parser

function Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	return setmetatable({ tokens = tokens, pos = 1, variables = variables }, Parser)
end

function Parser:peek()
	return self.tokens[self.pos].kind
end

function Parser:take(kind)
	local token = self.tokens[self.pos]
	if kind and token.kind ~= kind then
		error(`expected {kind}, got {token.kind}`, 0)
	end
	self.pos += 1
	return token
end

local PRECEDENCE = { ["+"] = 1, ["-"] = 1, ["*"] = 2, ["/"] = 2, ["^"] = 3 }

function Parser:primary()
	local token = self:take()
	if token.kind == "number" then
		return token.value
	elseif token.kind == "name" then
		local value = self.variables[token.value]
		if value == nil then
			error(`unknown variable {token.value}`, 0)
		end
		return value
	elseif token.kind == "-" then
		return -self:expression(3)
	elseif token.kind == "(" then
		local value = self:expression(0)
		self:take(")")
		return value
	end
	error(`unexpected {token.kind}`, 0)
end

function Parser:expression(minimum)
	local left = self:primary()
	while true do
		local op = self:peek()
		local precedence = PRECEDENCE[op]
		if not precedence or precedence <= minimum and op ~= "^" or precedence < minimum then
			return left
		end
		self:take()
		local right = self:expression(op == "^" and precedence - 1 or precedence)
		if op == "+" then
			left += right
		elseif op == "-" then
			left -= right
		elseif op == "*" then
			left *= right
		elseif op == "/" then
			if right == 0 then
				error("division by zero", 0)
			end
			left /= right
		else
			left ^= right
		end
	end
end

local function run(line, variables)
	local tokens = tokenize(line)
	local target
	if tokens[2].kind == "=" then
		target = tokens[1].value
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
	end
	local parser = Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	local value = parser:expression(0)
	parser:take("end")
	if target then
		variables[target] = value
	end
	return value
end

local variables = { pi = math.pi }
for _, line in { "x = 2 + 3 * 4", "y = (x - 4) ^ 2 / 2", "x * y - -3", "r = 2", "pi * r ^ 2", "1 / (x - 14)", "z + 1", "3 $ 4" } do
	local ok, result = pcall(run, line, variables)
	print(line, "=>", if ok then string.format("%.4g", result) else `error: {result}`)
end

-- A tokenizer and recursive-descent parser for arithmetic, with variables and errors.

local function tokenize(source)
	local tokens = {}
	local i = 1
	while i <= #source do
		local c = source:sub(i, i)
		if c:match("%s") then
			i += 1
		elseif c:match("%d") then
			local number = source:match("^%d+%.?%d*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "number", value = tonumber(number) })
			i += #number
		elseif c:match("[%a_]") then
			local name = source:match("^[%a_][%w_]*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "name", value = name })
			i += #name
		elseif c:match("[%+%-%*/%^%(%)=]") then
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = c })
			i += 1
		else
			error(`unexpected character '{c}' at {i}`, 0)
		end
	end
	table.insert(tokens, { kind = "end" })
	return tokens
end

local Parser = {}
Parser.__index = Parser

function Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	return setmetatable({ tokens = tokens, pos = 1, variables = variables }, Parser)
end

function Parser:peek()
	return self.tokens[self.pos].kind
end

function Parser:take(kind)
	local token = self.tokens[self.pos]
	if kind and token.kind ~= kind then
		error(`expected {kind}, got {token.kind}`, 0)
	end
	self.pos += 1
	return token
end

local PRECEDENCE = { ["+"] = 1, ["-"] = 1, ["*"] = 2, ["/"] = 2, ["^"] = 3 }

function Parser:primary()
	local token = self:take()
	if token.kind == "number" then
		return token.value
	elseif token.kind == "name" then
		local value = self.variables[token.value]
		if value == nil then
			error(`unknown variable {token.value}`, 0)
		end
		return value
	elseif token.kind == "-" then
		return -self:expression(3)
	elseif token.kind == "(" then
		local value = self:expression(0)
		self:take(")")
		return value
	end
	error(`unexpected {token.kind}`, 0)
end

function Parser:expression(minimum)
	local left = self:primary()
	while true do
		local op = self:peek()
		local precedence = PRECEDENCE[op]
		if not precedence or precedence <= minimum and op ~= "^" or precedence < minimum then
			return left
		end
		self:take()
		local right = self:expression(op == "^" and precedence - 1 or precedence)
		if op == "+" then
			left += right
		elseif op == "-" then
			left -= right
		elseif op == "*" then
			left *= right
		elseif op == "/" then
			if right == 0 then
				error("division by zero", 0)
			end
			left /= right
		else
			left ^= right
		end
	end
end

local function run(line, variables)
	local tokens = tokenize(line)
	local target
	if tokens[2].kind == "=" then
		target = tokens[1].value
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
	end
	local parser = Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	local value = parser:expression(0)
	parser:take("end")
	if target then
		variables[target] = value
	end
	return value
end

local variables = { pi = math.pi }
for _, line in { "x = 2 + 3 * 4", "y = (x - 4) ^ 2 / 2", "x * y - -3", "r = 2", "pi * r ^ 2", "1 / (x - 14)", "z + 1", "3 $ 4" } do
	local ok, result = pcall(run, line, variables)
	print(line, "=>", if ok then string.format("%.4g", result) else `error: {result}`)
end

-- A tokenizer and recursive-descent parser for arithmetic, with variables and errors.

local function tokenize(source)
	local tokens = {}
	local i = 1
	while i <= #source do
		local c = source:sub(i, i)
		if c:match("%s") then
			i += 1
		elseif c:match("%d") then
			local number = source:match("^%d+%.?%d*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "number", value = tonumber(number) })
			i += #number
		elseif c:match("[%a_]") then
			local name = source:match("^[%a_][%w_]*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "name", value = name })
			i += #name
		elseif c:match("[%+%-%*/%^%(%)=]") then
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = c })
			i += 1
		else
			error(`unexpected character '{c}' at {i}`, 0)
		end
	end
	table.insert(tokens, { kind = "end" })
	return tokens
end

local Parser = {}
Parser.__index = Parser

function Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	return setmetatable({ tokens = tokens, pos = 1, variables = variables }, Parser)
end

function Parser:peek()
	return self.tokens[self.pos].kind
end

function Parser:take(kind)
	local token = self.tokens[self.pos]
	if kind and token.kind ~= kind then
		error(`expected {kind}, got {token.kind}`, 0)
	end
	self.pos += 1
	return token
end

local PRECEDENCE = { ["+"] = 1, ["-"] = 1, ["*"] = 2, ["/"] = 2, ["^"] = 3 }

function Parser:primary()
	local token = self:take()
	if token.kind == "number" then
		return token.value
	elseif token.kind == "name" then
		local value = self.variables[token.value]
		if value == nil then
			error(`unknown variable {token.value}`, 0)
		end
		return value
	elseif token.kind == "-" then
		return -self:expression(3)
	elseif token.kind == "(" then
		local value = self:expression(0)
		self:take(")")
		return value
	end
	error(`unexpected {token.kind}`, 0)
end

function Parser:expression(minimum)
	local left = self:primary()
	while true do
		local op = self:peek()
		local precedence = PRECEDENCE[op]
		if not precedence or precedence <= minimum and op ~= "^" or precedence < minimum then
			return left
		end
		self:take()
		local right = self:expression(op == "^" and precedence - 1 or precedence)
		if op == "+" then
			left += right
		elseif op == "-" then
			left -= right
		elseif op == "*" then
			left *= right
		elseif op == "/" then
			if right == 0 then
				error("division by zero", 0)
			end
			left /= right
		else
			left ^= right
		end
	end
end

local function run(line, variables)
	local tokens = tokenize(line)
	local target
	if tokens[2].kind == "=" then
		target = tokens[1].value
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
	end
	local parser = Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	local value = parser:expression(0)
	parser:take("end")
	if target then
		variables[target] = value
	end
	return value
end

local variables = { pi = math.pi }
for _, line in { "x = 2 + 3 * 4", "y = (x - 4) ^ 2 / 2", "x * y - -3", "r = 2", "pi * r ^ 2", "1 / (x - 14)", "z + 1", "3 $ 4" } do
	local ok, result = pcall(run, line, variables)
	print(line, "=>", if ok then string.format("%.4g", result) else `error: {result}`)
end

-- A tokenizer and recursive-descent parser for arithmetic, with variables and errors.

local function tokenize(source)
	local tokens = {}
	local i = 1
	while i <= #source do
		local c = source:sub(i, i)
		if c:match("%s") then
			i += 1
		elseif c:match("%d") then
			local number = source:match("^%d+%.?%d*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "number", value = tonumber(number) })
			i += #number
		elseif c:match("[%a_]") then
			local name = source:match("^[%a_][%w_]*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "name", value = name })
			i += #name
		elseif c:match("[%+%-%*/%^%(%)=]") then
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = c })
			i += 1
		else
			error(`unexpected character '{c}' at {i}`, 0)
		end
	end
	table.insert(tokens, { kind = "end" })
	return tokens
end

local Parser = {}
Parser.__index = Parser

function Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	return setmetatable({ tokens = tokens, pos = 1, variables = variables }, Parser)
end

function Parser:peek()
	return self.tokens[self.pos].kind
end

function Parser:take(kind)
	local token = self.tokens[self.pos]
	if kind and token.kind ~= kind then
		error(`expected {kind}, got {token.kind}`, 0)
	end
	self.pos += 1
	return token
end

local PRECEDENCE = { ["+"] = 1, ["-"] = 1, ["*"] = 2, ["/"] = 2, ["^"] = 3 }

function Parser:primary()
	local token = self:take()
	if token.kind == "number" then
		return token.value
	elseif token.kind == "name" then
		local value = self.variables[token.value]
		if value == nil then
			error(`unknown variable {token.value}`, 0)
		end
		return value
	elseif token.kind == "-" then
		return -self:expression(3)
	elseif token.kind == "(" then
		local value = self:expression(0)
		self:take(")")
		return value
	end
	error(`unexpected {token.kind}`, 0)
end

function Parser:expression(minimum)
	local left = self:primary()
	while true do
		local op = self:peek()
		local precedence = PRECEDENCE[op]
		if not precedence or precedence <= minimum and op ~= "^" or precedence < minimum then
			return left
		end
		self:take()
		local right = self:expression(op == "^" and precedence - 1 or precedence)
		if op == "+" then
			left += right
		elseif op == "-" then
			left -= right
		elseif op == "*" then
			left *= right
		elseif op == "/" then
			if right == 0 then
				error("division by zero", 0)
			end
			left /= right
		else
			left ^= right
		end
	end
end

local function run(line, variables)
	local tokens = tokenize(line)
	local target
	if tokens[2].kind == "=" then
		target = tokens[1].value
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
	end
	local parser = Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	local value = parser:expression(0)
	parser:take("end")
	if target then
		variables[target] = value
	end
	return value
end

local variables = { pi = math.pi }
for _, line in { "x = 2 + 3 * 4", "y = (x - 4) ^ 2 / 2", "x * y - -3", "r = 2", "pi * r ^ 2", "1 / (x - 14)", "z + 1", "3 $ 4" } do
	local ok, result = pcall(run, line, variables)
	print(line, "=>", if ok then string.format("%.4g", result) else `error: {result}`)
end

-- upvalues, nested closures and recursion
local function makeCounter(start, step)
	local value = start
	return function()
		value += step
		return value
	end, function()
		value = start
	end
end

local next, reset = makeCounter(10, 5)
print(next(), next())
reset()
print(next())

local function memoize(fn)
	local cache = {}
	return function(n)
		local hit = cache[n]
		if hit == nil then
			hit = fn(n)
			cache[n] = hit
		end
		return hit
	end
end

local fib
fib = memoize(function(n)
	if n < 2 then
		return n
	end
	return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
end)
print(fib(40))

local handlers = {}
for i = 1, 3 do
	handlers[i] = function(x)
		return x * i
	end
end
print(handlers[2](21))

-- upvalues, nested closures and recursion
local function makeCounter(start, step)
	local value = start
	return function()
		value += step
		return value
	end, function()
		value = start
	end
end

local next, reset = makeCounter(10, 5)
print(next(), next())
reset()
print(next())

local function memoize(fn)
	local cache = {}
	return function(n)
		local hit = cache[n]
		if hit == nil then
			hit = fn(n)
			cache[n] = hit
		end
		return hit
	end
end

local fib
fib = memoize(function(n)
	if n < 2 then
		return n
	end
	return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
end)

-- upvalues, nested closures and recursion
local function makeCounter(start, step)
	local value = start
	return function()
		value += step
		return value
	end, function()
		value = start
	end
end

local next, reset = makeCounter(10, 5)
print(next(), next())
reset()
print(next())

local function memoize(fn)
	local cache = {}
	return function(n)
		local hit = cache[n]
		if hit == nil then
			hit = fn(n)
			cache[n] = hit
		end
		return hit
	end
end

local fib
fib = memoize(function(n)
	if n < 2 then
		return n
	end
	return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
end)
print(fib(40))

local handlers = {}
for i = 1, 3 do
	handlers[i] = function(x)
		return x * i
	end
end
print(handlers[2](21))

-- branches and every loop kind
local function classify(n)
	if n < 0 then
		return "negative"
	elseif n == 0 then
		return "zero"
	elseif n % 2 == 0 then
		return "even"
	else
		return "odd"
	end
end

local function sumUntil(limit)
	local total, i = 0, 1
	while total < limit do
		total += i
		i += 1
	end
	return total, i
end

local function firstPrimeAfter(n)
	local candidate = n
	repeat
		candidate += 1
		local prime = candidate > 1
		for d = 2, math.floor(math.sqrt(candidate)) do
			if candidate % d == 0 then
				prime = false
				break
			end
		end
	until prime
	return candidate
end

local counts = {}
for _, word in ipairs({ "a", "b", "a", "c", "b", "a" }) do
	if word == "c" then
		continue
	end
	counts[word] = (counts[word] or 0) + 1
end

for key, value in pairs(counts) do
	print(key, value, classify(value))
end

for i = 10, 1, -3 do
	print(i, sumUntil(i), firstPrimeAfter(i))
end

local function classify(n)
	if n < 0 then
		return "negative"

		return "zero"
	elseif n % 2 == 0 then
		return "even"
	else
		return "odd"
	end
end

local function sumUntil(limit)
	local total, i = 0, 1
	while total < limit do
		total += i
		i += 1
	end
	return total, i
end

local function firstPrimeAfter(n)
	local candidate = n
	repeat
		candidate += 1
		local prime = candidate > 1
		for d = 2, math.floor(math.sqrt(candidate)) do
			if candidate % d == 0 then
				prime = false
				break
			end
		end
	until prime
	return candidate
end

-- branches and every loop kind
local function classify(n)
	if n < 0 then
		return "negative"
	elseif n == 0 then
		return "zero"
	elseif n % 2 == 0 then
		return "even"
	else
		return "odd"
	end
end

local function sumUntil(limit)
	local total, i = 0, 1
	while total < limit do
		total += i
		i += 1
	end
	return total, i
end

local function firstPrimeAfter(n)
	local candidate = n
	repeat
		candidate += 1
		local prime = candidate > 1
		for d = 2, math.floor(math.sqrt(candidate)) do
			if candidate % d == 0 then
				prime = false
				break
			end
		end
	until prime
	return candidate
end

local counts = {}
for _, word in ipairs({ "a", "b", "a", "c", "b", "a" }) do
	if word == "c" then
		continue
	end
	counts[word] = (counts[word] or 0) + 1
end

for key, value in pairs(counts) do
	print(key, value, classify(value))
end

for i = 10, 1, -3 do
	print(i, sumUntil(i), firstPrimeAfter(i))
end

	local dx = bx - ax
	local dy = by - ay
	return math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)

local waypoints = { { 0, 0 }, { 3, 4 }, { 6, 8 } }
local travelled = 0
for index = 2, #waypoints do
	local previous = waypoints[index - 1]
	local current = waypoints[index]
	travelled += distance(previous[1], previous[2], current[1], current[2])
end
print(travelled)

end

-- compiled with debug level 2, so the real local names are in the bytecode
local function distance(ax, ay, bx, by)
	local dx = bx - ax
	local dy = by - ay
	return math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
end

local waypoints = { { 0, 0 }, { 3, 4 }, { 6, 8 } }
local travelled = 0
for index = 2, #waypoints do
	local previous = waypoints[index - 1]
	local current = waypoints[index]
	travelled += distance(previous[1], previous[2], current[1], current[2])
end
print(travelled)

-- branch-heavy code (a friend's challenge): ifs nested 150 deep, 300 if/elseif/else in a row and
-- 300 conditions with a dead `false and` part. A decompiler that retries a nested `if` on a
-- failed attempt takes 2^depth steps here
local n = tonumber("3")
local out = {}
if n + 0 > 0 then
	table.insert(out, 0)
	if n + 1 > 1 then
		table.insert(out, 1)
		if n + 2 > 2 then
			table.insert(out, 2)
			if n + 3 > 3 then

-- evaluation order a decompiler can't move: locals used once whose calls have side effects,
-- the operands of > and >= (compiled as < and <= with the operands swapped), a method call's
-- object and arguments, and values read before a later write or call changes them
local trace = {}
local function note(tag, value)
	table.insert(trace, tag)
	return value
end
local function flush(label)
	print(label, table.concat(trace, " "))
	table.clear(trace)
end

-- two locals used once each, in the opposite order: inlining both would swap the calls
local first = note("a", 1)
local second = note("b", 2)
print(second, first)
flush("locals")

-- > and >= compile to LT and LE with the operands swapped, but they still run left to right
print(note("l", 3) > note("r", 2), note("l", 1) >= note("r", 1), note("l", "x") < note("r", "y"))
flush("compare")
print(not (note("l", 1) <= note("r", 2)), note("l", 2) ~= note("r", 2))
flush("compare not")
if note("cond l", 5) > note("cond r", 4) then
	note("then", nil)
end
flush("branch")

-- the object of a method call is worked out once, before its arguments
local obj = { n = 0 }
function obj:add(k)
	self.n += k
	return self
end
local function getobj()
	note("obj", nil)
	return obj
end
getobj():add(note("arg", 1)):add(note("arg2", 2))
print(obj.n)
flush("method")

-- a value read into a local before the table changes keeps the old value
local t = { v = "old" }
local saved = t.v
t.v = "new"
print(saved, t.v)
local box = { 1, 2, 3 }
local len = #box
table.insert(box, 4)
print(len, #box)

-- a call that changes a local the same argument list reads before and after it
local counter = 0
local function bump()
	counter += 1
	return counter
end
print(counter, bump(), counter + 0, bump())
local before = counter
bump()
print(before, counter)

-- an index read before a call in the same expression moves it
local arr = { 10, 20, 30 }
local i = 1
local function advance()
	i += 1
	return 0
end
print(arr[i] + advance(), arr[i])

-- every operand runs left to right before anything combines, right-associative or not
print(note("1", "a") .. note("2", "b") .. note("3", "c"))
flush("concat")
print(note("x", 2) ^ note("y", 3) ^ note("z", 1), note("p", 10) - note("q", 3) - note("r", 2))
flush("arith")

-- and / or only run what they need
local hit = note("left", false) and note("never", true) or note("right", "ok")
print(hit)
flush("logic")

-- a constructor evaluates its entries in order, keyed or not
local made = { note("one", 1), k = note("key", 2), note("two", 3), [note("ikey", "x")] = note("ival", 4) }
print(made[1], made[2], made.k, made.x)
flush("constructor")

-- an assignment reads its target table before the right-hand side runs, so a call that replaces
-- the table writes into the old one
local holder = { inner = { v = 0 } }
local function swap()
	note("swap", nil)
	local old = holder.inner
	holder.inner = { v = 100 }
	return old.v + 1
end
holder.inner.v = swap()
print(holder.inner.v)
flush("target")

entries.source:
-- evaluation order a decompiler can't move: locals used once whose calls have side effects,
-- the operands of > and >= (compiled as < and <= with the operands swapped), a method call's
-- object and arguments, and values read before a later write or call changes them
local trace = {}
local function note(tag, value)
	table.insert(trace, tag)
	return value
end
local function flush(label)
	print(label, table.concat(trace, " "))
	table.clear(trace)
end

-- two locals used once each, in the opposite order: inlining both would swap the calls
local first = note("a", 1)
local second = note("b", 2)
print(second, first)
flush("locals")

-- > and >= compile to LT and LE with the operands swapped, but they still run left to right
print(note("l", 3) > note("r", 2), note("l", 1) >= note("r", 1), note("l", "x") < note("r", "y"))
flush("compare")
print(not (note("l", 1) <= note("r", 2)), note("l", 2) ~= note("r", 2))
flush("compare not")
if note("cond l", 5) > note("cond r", 4) then
	note("then", nil)
end
flush("branch")

-- the object of a method call is worked out once, before its arguments
local obj = { n = 0 }
function obj:add(k)
	self.n += k
	return self
end
local function getobj()
	note("obj", nil)
	return obj
end
getobj():add(note("arg", 1)):add(note("arg2", 2))
print(obj.n)
flush("method")

-- a value read into a local before the table changes keeps the old value
local t = { v = "old" }
local saved = t.v
t.v = "new"
print(saved, t.v)
local box = { 1, 2, 3 }
local len = #box
table.insert(box, 4)
print(len, #box)

-- a call that changes a local the same argument list reads before and after it
local counter = 0
local function bump()
	counter += 1
	return counter
end
print(counter, bump(), counter + 0, bump())
local before = counter
bump()
print(before, counter)

-- an index read before a call in the same expression moves it
local arr = { 10, 20, 30 }
local i = 1
local function advance()
	i += 1
	return 0
end
print(arr[i] + advance(), arr[i])

-- every operand runs left to right before anything combines, right-associative or not
print(note("1", "a") .. note("2", "b") .. note("3", "c"))
flush("concat")
print(note("x", 2) ^ note("y", 3) ^ note("z", 1), note("p", 10) - note("q", 3) - note("r", 2))
flush("arith")

-- and / or only run what they need
local hit = note("left", false) and note("never", true) or note("right", "ok")
print(hit)
flush("logic")

-- a constructor evaluates its entries in order, keyed or not
local made = { note("one", 1), k = note("key", 2), note("two", 3), [note("ikey", "x")] = note("ival", 4) }
print(made[1], made[2], made.k, made.x)
flush("constructor")

-- an assignment reads its target table before the right-hand side runs, so a call that replaces
-- the table writes into the old one
local holder = { inner = { v = 0 } }
local function swap()
	note("swap", nil)
	local old = holder.inner
	holder.inner = { v = 100 }
	return old.v + 1
end
holder.inner.v = swap()
print(holder.inner.v)
flush("target")

-- evaluation order a decompiler can't move: locals used once whose calls have side effects,
-- the operands of > and >= (compiled as < and <= with the operands swapped), a method call's
-- object and arguments, and values read before a later write or call changes them
local trace = {}
local function note(tag, value)
	table.insert(trace, tag)
	return value
end
local function flush(label)
	print(label, table.concat(trace, " "))
	table.clear(trace)
end

-- two locals used once each, in the opposite order: inlining both would swap the calls
local first = note("a", 1)
local second = note("b", 2)
print(second, first)
flush("locals")

-- > and >= compile to LT and LE with the operands swapped, but they still run left to right
print(note("l", 3) > note("r", 2), note("l", 1) >= note("r", 1), note("l", "x") < note("r", "y"))
flush("compare")
print(not (note("l", 1) <= note("r", 2)), note("l", 2) ~= note("r", 2))
flush("compare not")
if note("cond l", 5) > note("cond r", 4) then
	note("then", nil)
end
flush("branch")

-- the object of a method call is worked out once, before its arguments
local obj = { n = 0 }
function obj:add(k)
	self.n += k
	return self
end
local function getobj()
	note("obj", nil)
	return obj
end
getobj():add(note("arg", 1)):add(note("arg2", 2))
print(obj.n)
flush("method")

-- a value read into a local before the table changes keeps the old value
local t = { v = "old" }
local saved = t.v
t.v = "new"
print(saved, t.v)
local box = { 1, 2, 3 }
local len = #box
table.insert(box, 4)
print(len, #box)

-- a call that changes a local the same argument list reads before and after it
local counter = 0
local function bump()
	counter += 1
	return counter
end
print(counter, bump(), counter + 0, bump())
local before = counter
bump()
print(before, counter)

-- an index read before a call in the same expression moves it
local arr = { 10, 20, 30 }
local i = 1
local function advance()
	i += 1
	return 0
end
print(arr[i] + advance(), arr[i])

-- every operand runs left to right before anything combines, right-associative or not
print(note("1", "a") .. note("2", "b") .. note("3", "c"))
flush("concat")
print(note("x", 2) ^ note("y", 3) ^ note("z", 1), note("p", 10) - note("q", 3) - note("r", 2))
flush("arith")

-- and / or only run what they need
local hit = note("left", false) and note("never", true) or note("right", "ok")
print(hit)
flush("logic")

-- a constructor evaluates its entries in order, keyed or not
local made = { note("one", 1), k = note("key", 2), note("two", 3), [note("ikey", "x")] = note("ival", 4) }
print(made[1], made[2], made.k, made.x)
flush("constructor")

-- an assignment reads its target table before the right-hand side runs, so a call that replaces
-- the table writes into the old one
local holder = { inner = { v = 0 } }
local function swap()
	note("swap", nil)
	local old = holder.inner
	holder.inner = { v = 100 }
	return old.v + 1
end
holder.inner.v = swap()
print(holder.inner.v)
flush("target")

-- event handlers and loops over instance collections
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local function onCharacter(character)
	local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
	humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
		print(character.Name, "died")
	end)
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	print("joined", player.Name, player.UserId)
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacter)
	player.Chatted:Connect(function(message)
		if message == "/reset" and player.Character then
			player.Character:BreakJoints()
		end
	end)
end)

workspace.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child)
	if child:IsA("BasePart") then
		child.Anchored = true
	end
end)

local pad = workspace:WaitForChild("Pad")
pad.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
	local owner = Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
	if owner then
		print(owner.Name, "touched the pad")
	end
end)

UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessed)
	if not gameProcessed and input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.E then
		print("interact")
	end
end)

local elapsed = 0
RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(deltaTime)
	elapsed += deltaTime
end)

for _, child in ipairs(workspace:GetChildren()) do
	print(child.Name)
end

for _, descendant in workspace:GetDescendants() do
	if descendant:IsA("Light") then
		descendant.Enabled = false
	end
end

for _, player in pairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
	print(player.DisplayName, elapsed)
end

-- event handlers and loops over instance collections
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local function onCharacter(character)
	local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
	humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
		print(character.Name, "died")
	end)
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	print("joined", player.Name, player.UserId)
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacter)
	player.Chatted:Connect(function(message)
		if message == "/reset" and player.Character then
			player.Character:BreakJoints()
		end
	end)
end)

workspace.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child)
	if child:IsA("BasePart") then
		child.Anchored = true
	end
end)

local pad = workspace:WaitForChild("Pad")
pad.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
	local owner = Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
	if owner then
		print(owner.Name, "touched the pad")
	end
end)

UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessed)
	if not gameProcessed and input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.E then
		print("interact")
	end
end)

local elapsed = 0
RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(deltaTime)
	elapsed += deltaTime
end)

for _, child in ipairs(workspace:GetChildren()) do
	print(child.Name)
end

for _, descendant in workspace:GetDescendants() do
	if descendant:IsA("Light") then
		descendant.Enabled = false
	end
end

for _, player in pairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
	print(player.DisplayName, elapsed)
end

-- event handlers and loops over instance collections
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local function onCharacter(character)
	local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
	humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
		print(character.Name, "died")
	end)
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	print("joined", player.Name, player.UserId)
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacter)
	player.Chatted:Connect(function(message)
		if message == "/reset" and player.Character then
			player.Character:BreakJoints()
		end
	end)
end)

workspace.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child)
	if child:IsA("BasePart") then
		child.Anchored = true
	end
end)

local pad = workspace:WaitForChild("Pad")
pad.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
	local owner = Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
	if owner then
		print(owner.Name, "touched the pad")
	end
end)

UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessed)
	if not gameProcessed and input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.E then
		print("interact")
	end
end)

local elapsed = 0
RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(deltaTime)
	elapsed += deltaTime
end)

for _, child in ipairs(workspace:GetChildren()) do
	print(child.Name)
end

for _, descendant in workspace:GetDescendants() do
	if descendant:IsA("Light") then
		descendant.Enabled = false
	end
end

for _, player in pairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
	print(player.DisplayName, elapsed)
end

-- generic for without an iterator function: plain tables (array part, then hash part), __iter
-- returning a closure or next, objects with __call, coroutines, and pairs and ipairs, which the
-- compiler turns into their own loop instructions
local function keys(t)
	local out = {}
	for k in t do
		table.insert(out, tostring(k))
	end
	table.sort(out)
	return table.concat(out, ",")
end

local list = { "a", "b", "c" }
for i, v in list do
	print("plain", i, v)
end
for i, v in ipairs(list) do
	print("ipairs", i, v)
end
for i, v in pairs(list) do
	print("pairs", i, v)
end
print(keys({ x = 1, y = 2, [3] = true, [true] = 0 }))

-- a hole: ipairs stops at it, a plain loop and pairs walk past it
local holes = { 1, 2, nil, 4 }
local viaIpairs, viaPlain, viaPairs = 0, 0, 0
for _ in ipairs(holes) do
	viaIpairs += 1
end
for _ in holes do
	viaPlain += 1
end
for _ in pairs(holes) do
	viaPairs += 1
end
print(viaIpairs, viaPlain, viaPairs)

-- __iter returning a stateful closure
local Range = {}
Range.__index = Range
Range.__iter = function(self)
	local i = self.from - self.step
	return function()
		i += self.step
		if i <= self.to then
			return i, i * i
		end
		return nil
	end
end
local function range(from, to, step)
	return setmetatable({ from = from, to = to, step = step or 1 }, Range)
end
for v, sq in range(1, 7, 3) do
	print("range", v, sq)
end

-- __iter handing back next and another table to walk
local Bag = {
	__iter = function(self)
		return next, self.items
	end,
}
local bag = setmetatable({ items = { "x", "y" }, hidden = true }, Bag)
for k, v in bag do
	print("bag", k, v)
end

-- an object with __call is the iterator function itself
local countdown = setmetatable({ n = 3 }, {
	__call = function(self)
		if self.n > 0 then
			self.n -= 1
			return self.n + 1
		end
		return nil
	end,
})
for v in countdown do
	print("countdown", v)
end

-- a coroutine as the iterator
for v in coroutine.wrap(function()
	for i = 1, 3 do
		coroutine.yield(i * 2)
	end
end) do
	print("co", v)
end

-- continue, break and writing the loop variable inside generalized loops
for i, v in list do
	if v == "b" then
		continue
	end
	i *= 10
	print("skip b", i, v)
end
local found
for i, v in { 5, 6, 7, 8 } do
	if v % 2 == 1 and i > 1 then
		found = i
		break
	end
end
print("found", found)

-- nested loops over the same table, the inner one reading the outer's variables
local grid = { { 1, 2 }, { 3, 4 } }
local sum = 0
for r, row in grid do
	for c, cell in row do
		sum += cell * r * c
	end
end
print("grid", sum)

-- a table changed between loops is walked as it is now
local growing = { 1 }
for round = 1, 3 do
	local seen = 0
	for _ in growing do
		seen += 1
	end
	growing[#growing + 1] = round
	print("round", round, seen)
end

-- generic for without an iterator function: plain tables (array part, then hash part), __iter
-- returning a closure or next, objects with __call, coroutines, and pairs and ipairs, which the
-- compiler turns into their own loop instructions
local function keys(t)
	local out = {}
	for k in t do
		table.insert(out, tostring(k))
	end
	table.sort(out)
	return table.concat(out, ",")
end

local list = { "a", "b", "c" }
for i, v in list do
	print("plain", i, v)
end
for i, v in ipairs(list) do
	print("ipairs", i, v)
end
for i, v in pairs(list) do
	print("pairs", i, v)
end
print(keys({ x = 1, y = 2, [3] = true, [true] = 0 }))

-- a hole: ipairs stops at it, a plain loop and pairs walk past it
local holes = { 1, 2, nil, 4 }
local viaIpairs, viaPlain, viaPairs = 0, 0, 0
for _ in ipairs(holes) do
	viaIpairs += 1
end
for _ in holes do
	viaPlain += 1
end
for _ in pairs(holes) do
	viaPairs += 1
end
print(viaIpairs, viaPlain, viaPairs)

-- __iter returning a stateful closure
local Range = {}
Range.__index = Range
Range.__iter = function(self)
	local i = self.from - self.step
	return function()
		i += self.step
		if i <= self.to then
			return i, i * i
		end
		return nil
	end
end
local function range(from, to, step)
	return setmetatable({ from = from, to = to, step = step or 1 }, Range)
end
for v, sq in range(1, 7, 3) do
	print("range", v, sq)
end

-- __iter handing back next and another table to walk
local Bag = {
	__iter = function(self)
		return next, self.items
	end,
}
local bag = setmetatable({ items = { "x", "y" }, hidden = true }, Bag)
for k, v in bag do
	print("bag", k, v)
end

-- an object with __call is the iterator function itself
local countdown = setmetatable({ n = 3 }, {
	__call = function(self)
		if self.n > 0 then
			self.n -= 1
			return self.n + 1
		end
		return nil
	end,
})
for v in countdown do
	print("countdown", v)
end

-- a coroutine as the iterator
for v in coroutine.wrap(function()
	for i = 1, 3 do
		coroutine.yield(i * 2)
	end
end) do
	print("co", v)
end

-- continue, break and writing the loop variable inside generalized loops
for i, v in list do
	if v == "b" then
		continue
	end
	i *= 10
	print("skip b", i, v)
end
local found
for i, v in { 5, 6, 7, 8 } do
	if v % 2 == 1 and i > 1 then
		found = i
		break
	end
end
print("found", found)

-- nested loops over the same table, the inner one reading the outer's variables
local grid = { { 1, 2 }, { 3, 4 } }
local sum = 0
for r, row in grid do
	for c, cell in row do
		sum += cell * r * c
	end
end
print("grid", sum)

-- a table changed between loops is walked as it is now
local growing = { 1 }
for round = 1, 3 do
	local seen = 0
	for _ in growing do
		seen += 1
	end
	growing[#growing + 1] = round
	print("round", round, seen)
end

-- generic for without an iterator function: plain tables (array part, then hash part), __iter
-- returning a closure or next, objects with __call, coroutines, and pairs and ipairs, which the
-- compiler turns into their own loop instructions
local function keys(t)
	local out = {}
	for k in t do
		table.insert(out, tostring(k))
	end
	table.sort(out)
	return table.concat(out, ",")
end

local list = { "a", "b", "c" }
for i, v in list do
	print("plain", i, v)
end
for i, v in ipairs(list) do
	print("ipairs", i, v)
end
for i, v in pairs(list) do
	print("pairs", i, v)
end
print(keys({ x = 1, y = 2, [3] = true, [true] = 0 }))

-- a hole: ipairs stops at it, a plain loop and pairs walk past it
local holes = { 1, 2, nil, 4 }
local viaIpairs, viaPlain, viaPairs = 0, 0, 0
for _ in ipairs(holes) do
	viaIpairs += 1
end
for _ in holes do
	viaPlain += 1
end
for _ in pairs(holes) do
	viaPairs += 1
end
print(viaIpairs, viaPlain, viaPairs)

-- __iter returning a stateful closure
local Range = {}
Range.__index = Range
Range.__iter = function(self)
	local i = self.from - self.step
	return function()
		i += self.step
		if i <= self.to then
			return i, i * i
		end
		return nil
	end
end
local function range(from, to, step)
	return setmetatable({ from = from, to = to, step = step or 1 }, Range)
end
for v, sq in range(1, 7, 3) do
	print("range", v, sq)
end

-- __iter handing back next and another table to walk
local Bag = {
	__iter = function(self)
		return next, self.items

-- small local functions that -O2 copies into their callers
local log = {}

local function tap(tag, value)
	table.insert(log, tag)
	return value
end

local function clamp(x, lo, hi)
	if x < lo then
		return lo
	elseif x > hi then
		return hi
	end
	return x
end

local function guard(value)
	if not value then
		return
	end
	table.insert(log, "guarded " .. tostring(value))
end

local counter = 0
local function bump(by)
	counter += by
end

local sum = tap("l", 1) + tap("r", 2) * tap("m", 3)
local short = tap("p", false) and tap("q", 1) or tap("z", 2)
local tbl = {}
tbl[tap("ck", "count")] = (tbl.count or 0) + tap("cv", 1)

for i = -2, 12, 5 do
	print(i, clamp(i, 0, 10))
	bump(i)
end

guard(nil)
guard("yes")

local function scaled(n)
	return clamp(n * 2, 1, 9)
end

if clamp(sum, 0, 5) == 5 and scaled(3) > 4 then
	print("both")
end

while counter > 0 do
	counter -= clamp(counter, 1, 7)
	if counter % 3 == 0 then
		break
	end
end

print(sum, short, tbl.count, counter, table.concat(log, ","))

entries.source:
-- small local functions that -O2 copies into their callers
local log = {}

local function tap(tag, value)
	table.insert(log, tag)
	return value
end

local function clamp(x, lo, hi)
	if x < lo then
		return lo
	elseif x > hi then
		return hi
	end
	return x
end

local function guard(value)
	if not value then
		return
	end
	table.insert(log, "guarded " .. tostring(value))
end

local counter = 0
local function bump(by)
	counter += by
end

local sum = tap("l", 1) + tap("r", 2) * tap("m", 3)
local short = tap("p", false) and tap("q", 1) or tap("z", 2)
local tbl = {}
tbl[tap("ck", "count")] = (tbl.count or 0) + tap("cv", 1)

for i = -2, 12, 5 do
	print(i, clamp(i, 0, 10))
	bump(i)
end

guard(nil)
guard("yes")

local function scaled(n)
	return clamp(n * 2, 1, 9)
end

if clamp(sum, 0, 5) == 5 and scaled(3) > 4 then
	print("both")
end

while counter > 0 do
	counter -= clamp(counter, 1, 7)
	if counter % 3 == 0 then
		break
	end
end

print(sum, short, tbl.count, counter, table.concat(log, ","))

-- small local functions that -O2 copies into their callers
local log = {}

local function tap(tag, value)
	table.insert(log, tag)
	return value
end

local function clamp(x, lo, hi)
	if x < lo then
		return lo
	elseif x > hi then
		return hi
	end
	return x
end

local function guard(value)
	if not value then
		return
	end
	table.insert(log, "guarded " .. tostring(value))
end

local counter = 0
local function bump(by)
	counter += by
end

local sum = tap("l", 1) + tap("r", 2) * tap("m", 3)
local short = tap("p", false) and tap("q", 1) or tap("z", 2)
local tbl = {}
tbl[tap("ck", "count")] = (tbl.count or 0) + tap("cv", 1)

for i = -2, 12, 5 do
	print(i, clamp(i, 0, 10))
	bump(i)
end

guard(nil)
guard("yes")

local function scaled(n)
	return clamp(n * 2, 1, 9)
end

if clamp(sum, 0, 5) == 5 and scaled(3) > 4 then
	print("both")
end

while counter > 0 do
	counter -= clamp(counter, 1, 7)
	if counter % 3 == 0 then
		break
	end
end

print(sum, short, tbl.count, counter, table.concat(log, ","))

	if x < lo then

		return hi
	end

	if not value then

-- small local functions that -O2 copies into their callers
local log = {}

local function tap(tag, value)
	table.insert(log, tag)
	return value
end

local function clamp(x, lo, hi)
	if x < lo then
		return lo
	elseif x > hi then
		return hi
	end
	return x
end

local function guard(value)
	if not value then
		return
	end
	table.insert(log, "guarded " .. tostring(value))
end

local counter = 0
local function bump(by)
	counter += by
end

local sum = tap("l", 1) + tap("r", 2) * tap("m", 3)
local short = tap("p", false) and tap("q", 1) or tap("z", 2)
local tbl = {}
tbl[tap("ck", "count")] = (tbl.count or 0) + tap("cv", 1)

for i = -2, 12, 5 do
	print(i, clamp(i, 0, 10))
	bump(i)
end

guard(nil)
guard("yes")

local function scaled(n)
	return clamp(n * 2, 1, 9)
end

if clamp(sum, 0, 5) == 5 and scaled(3) > 4 then
	print("both")
end

while counter > 0 do
	counter -= clamp(counter, 1, 7)
	if counter % 3 == 0 then
		break
	end
end

print(sum, short, tbl.count, counter, table.concat(log, ","))

--!strict
-- An inventory with stacking, weight limits and a sorted report.

local Inventory = {}
Inventory.__index = Inventory

local ITEMS = {
	sword = { weight = 8, stack = 1, value = 120 },
	potion = { weight = 1, stack = 10, value = 25 },
	arrow = { weight = 0.1, stack = 64, value = 1 },
	shield = { weight = 12, stack = 1, value = 90 },
}

function Inventory.new(capacity)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Inventory)
	self.capacity = capacity
	self.slots = {}
	self.weight = 0
	return self
end

local function round(n, places)
	local scale = 10 ^ places
	return math.floor(n * scale + 0.5) / scale
end

function Inventory:add(name, count)
	local info = ITEMS[name]
	if not info then
		return false, `unknown item {name}`
	end
	if self.weight + info.weight * count > self.capacity then
		return false, `too heavy: {round(self.weight + info.weight * count, 1)} > {self.capacity}`
	end
	local left = count
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		if slot.name == name and slot.count < info.stack then
			local moved = math.min(info.stack - slot.count, left)
			slot.count += moved
			left -= moved
			if left == 0 then
				break
			end
		end
	end
	while left > 0 do
		local moved = math.min(info.stack, left)
		table.insert(self.slots, { name = name, count = moved })
		left -= moved
	end
	self.weight += info.weight * count
	return true
end

function Inventory:remove(name, count)
	for i = #self.slots, 1, -1 do
		local slot = self.slots[i]
		if slot.name ~= name then
			continue
		end
		local taken = math.min(slot.count, count)
		slot.count -= taken
		count -= taken
		self.weight -= ITEMS[name].weight * taken
		if slot.count == 0 then
			table.remove(self.slots, i)
		end
		if count == 0 then
			return true
		end
	end
	return count == 0
end

function Inventory:report()
	local totals = {}
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		totals[slot.name] = (totals[slot.name] or 0) + slot.count
	end
	local names = {}
	for name in totals do
		table.insert(names, name)
	end
	table.sort(names, function(a, b)
		return ITEMS[a].value * totals[a] > ITEMS[b].value * totals[b]
	end)
	local lines = {}
	for rank, name in names do
		lines[rank] = `{rank}. {name} x{totals[name]} ({ITEMS[name].value * totals[name]}g)`
	end
	return table.concat(lines, "\n"), round(self.weight, 2)
end

local bag = Inventory.new(40)
print(bag:add("arrow", 150))
print(bag:add("potion", 12))
print(bag:add("sword", 1))
print(bag:add("shield", 3))
print(bag:add("wand", 1))
print(bag:remove("arrow", 70), bag:remove("potion", 20))
print(bag:report())

--!strict
-- An inventory with stacking, weight limits and a sorted report.

local Inventory = {}
Inventory.__index = Inventory

local ITEMS = {
	sword = { weight = 8, stack = 1, value = 120 },
	potion = { weight = 1, stack = 10, value = 25 },
	arrow = { weight = 0.1, stack = 64, value = 1 },
	shield = { weight = 12, stack = 1, value = 90 },
}

function Inventory.new(capacity)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Inventory)
	self.capacity = capacity
	self.slots = {}
	self.weight = 0
	return self
end

local function round(n, places)
	local scale = 10 ^ places
	return math.floor(n * scale + 0.5) / scale
end

function Inventory:add(name, count)
	local info = ITEMS[name]
	if not info then
		return false, `unknown item {name}`
	end
	if self.weight + info.weight * count > self.capacity then
		return false, `too heavy: {round(self.weight + info.weight * count, 1)} > {self.capacity}`
	end
	local left = count
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		if slot.name == name and slot.count < info.stack then
			local moved = math.min(info.stack - slot.count, left)
			slot.count += moved
			left -= moved
			if left == 0 then
				break
			end
		end
	end
	while left > 0 do
		local moved = math.min(info.stack, left)
		table.insert(self.slots, { name = name, count = moved })
		left -= moved
	end
	self.weight += info.weight * count
	return true
end

function Inventory:remove(name, count)
	for i = #self.slots, 1, -1 do
		local slot = self.slots[i]
		if slot.name ~= name then
			continue
		end
		local taken = math.min(slot.count, count)
		slot.count -= taken
		count -= taken
		self.weight -= ITEMS[name].weight * taken
		if slot.count == 0 then
			table.remove(self.slots, i)
		end
		if count == 0 then
			return true
		end
	end
	return count == 0
end

function Inventory:report()
	local totals = {}
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		totals[slot.name] = (totals[slot.name] or 0) + slot.count
	end
	local names = {}
	for name in totals do
		table.insert(names, name)
	end
	table.sort(names, function(a, b)
		return ITEMS[a].value * totals[a] > ITEMS[b].value * totals[b]
	end)
	local lines = {}
	for rank, name in names do
		lines[rank] = `{rank}. {name} x{totals[name]} ({ITEMS[name].value * totals[name]}g)`
	end
	return table.concat(lines, "\n"), round(self.weight, 2)
end

local bag = Inventory.new(40)
print(bag:add("arrow", 150))
print(bag:add("potion", 12))
print(bag:add("sword", 1))
print(bag:add("shield", 3))
print(bag:add("wand", 1))
print(bag:remove("arrow", 70), bag:remove("potion", 20))
print(bag:report())

--!strict
-- An inventory with stacking, weight limits and a sorted report.

local Inventory = {}
Inventory.__index = Inventory

local ITEMS = {
	sword = { weight = 8, stack = 1, value = 120 },
	potion = { weight = 1, stack = 10, value = 25 },
	arrow = { weight = 0.1, stack = 64, value = 1 },
	shield = { weight = 12, stack = 1, value = 90 },
}

function Inventory.new(capacity)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Inventory)
	self.capacity = capacity
	self.slots = {}
	self.weight = 0
	return self
end

local function round(n, places)
	local scale = 10 ^ places
	return math.floor(n * scale + 0.5) / scale
end

function Inventory:add(name, count)
	local info = ITEMS[name]
	if not info then
		return false, `unknown item {name}`
	end
	if self.weight + info.weight * count > self.capacity then
		return false, `too heavy: {round(self.weight + info.weight * count, 1)} > {self.capacity}`
	end
	local left = count
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		if slot.name == name and slot.count < info.stack then
			local moved = math.min(info.stack - slot.count, left)
			slot.count += moved
			left -= moved
			if left == 0 then
				break
			end
		end
	end
	while left > 0 do
		local moved = math.min(info.stack, left)
		table.insert(self.slots, { name = name, count = moved })
		left -= moved
	end
	self.weight += info.weight * count
	return true
end

function Inventory:remove(name, count)
	for i = #self.slots, 1, -1 do
		local slot = self.slots[i]
		if slot.name ~= name then
			continue
		end
		local taken = math.min(slot.count, count)
		slot.count -= taken
		count -= taken
		self.weight -= ITEMS[name].weight * taken
		if slot.count == 0 then
			table.remove(self.slots, i)
		end
		if count == 0 then
			return true
		end
	end
	return count == 0
end

function Inventory:report()
	local totals = {}
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		totals[slot.name] = (totals[slot.name] or 0) + slot.count
	end
	local names = {}
	for name in totals do
		table.insert(names, name)
	end
	table.sort(names, function(a, b)
		return ITEMS[a].value * totals[a] > ITEMS[b].value * totals[b]
	end)
	local lines = {}
	for rank, name in names do
		lines[rank] = `{rank}. {name} x{totals[name]} ({ITEMS[name].value * totals[name]}g)`
	end
	return table.concat(lines, "\n"), round(self.weight, 2)
end

local bag = Inventory.new(40)
print(bag:add("arrow", 150))
print(bag:add("potion", 12))
print(bag:add("sword", 1))
print(bag:add("shield", 3))
print(bag:add("wand", 1))
print(bag:remove("arrow", 70), bag:remove("potion", 20))
print(bag:report())

--!strict
-- An inventory with stacking, weight limits and a sorted report.

local Inventory = {}
Inventory.__index = Inventory

local ITEMS = {
	sword = { weight = 8, stack = 1, value = 120 },
	potion = { weight = 1, stack = 10, value = 25 },
	arrow = { weight = 0.1, stack = 64, value = 1 },
	shield = { weight = 12, stack = 1, value = 90 },
}

function Inventory.new(capacity)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Inventory)
	self.capacity = capacity
	self.slots = {}
	self.weight = 0
	return self
end

local function round(n, places)
	local scale = 10 ^ places
	return math.floor(n * scale + 0.5) / scale
end

function Inventory:add(name, count)
	local info = ITEMS[name]
	if not info then
		return false, `unknown item {name}`
	end
	if self.weight + info.weight * count > self.capacity then
		return false, `too heavy: {round(self.weight + info.weight * count, 1)} > {self.capacity}`
	end
	local left = count
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		if slot.name == name and slot.count < info.stack then
			local moved = math.min(info.stack - slot.count, left)
			slot.count += moved
			left -= moved
			if left == 0 then
				break
			end
		end
	end
	while left > 0 do
		local moved = math.min(info.stack, left)
		table.insert(self.slots, { name = name, count = moved })
		left -= moved
	end
	self.weight += info.weight * count
	return true
end

function Inventory:remove(name, count)
	for i = #self.slots, 1, -1 do
		local slot = self.slots[i]
		if slot.name ~= name then
			continue
		end
		local taken = math.min(slot.count, count)
		slot.count -= taken
		count -= taken
		self.weight -= ITEMS[name].weight * taken
		if slot.count == 0 then
			table.remove(self.slots, i)
		end
		if count == 0 then
			return true
		end
	end
	return count == 0
end

function Inventory:report()
	local totals = {}
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		totals[slot.name] = (totals[slot.name] or 0) + slot.count
	end
	local names = {}
	for name in totals do
		table.insert(names, name)
	end
	table.sort(names, function(a, b)
		return ITEMS[a].value * totals[a] > ITEMS[b].value * totals[b]
	end)
	local lines = {}
	for rank, name in names do
		lines[rank] = `{rank}. {name} x{totals[name]} ({ITEMS[name].value * totals[name]}g)`
	end
	return table.concat(lines, "\n"), round(self.weight, 2)
end

local bag = Inventory.new(40)
print(bag:add("arrow", 150))
print(bag:add("potion", 12))
print(bag:add("sword", 1))
print(bag:add("shield", 3))
print(bag:add("wand", 1))
print(bag:remove("arrow", 70), bag:remove("potion", 20))
print(bag:report())

-- for loops: generic for over custom iterators (stateless, stateful, next directly), numeric for
-- with float and negative steps, bounds evaluated once, and a body that writes its loop variable
local function range(n)
	local i = 0
	return function()
		i += 1
		if i <= n then
			return i, i * i
		end
	end
end
for i, sq in range(3) do
	print("range", i, sq)
end

local function evens(t, i)
	i += 2
	if t[i] ~= nil then
		return i, t[i]
	end
end
local list = { "a", "b", "c", "d", "e" }
for i, v in evens, list, -1 do
	print("evens", i, v)
end

local sorted = { 10, 20, 30 }
for i, v in next, sorted do
	print("next", i, v)
end
for i, v in ipairs({ 1, 2, nil, 4 }) do
	print("ipairs", i, v)
end

for i = 1, 2, 0.5 do
	print("float", i)
end
for i = 3, 1, -1 do
	print("down", i)
end
for i = 1, 0 do
	print("never", i)
end
for i = 1.0, 3 do
	print("float start", i)
end

local calls = 0
local function bound(v)
	calls += 1
	return v

-- for loops: generic for over custom iterators (stateless, stateful, next directly), numeric for
-- with float and negative steps, bounds evaluated once, and a body that writes its loop variable
local function range(n)
	local i = 0
	return function()
		i += 1
		if i <= n then
			return i, i * i
		end
	end
end
for i, sq in range(3) do
	print("range", i, sq)
end

local function evens(t, i)
	i += 2
	if t[i] ~= nil then
		return i, t[i]
	end
end
local list = { "a", "b", "c", "d", "e" }
for i, v in evens, list, -1 do
	print("evens", i, v)
end

local sorted = { 10, 20, 30 }
for i, v in next, sorted do
	print("next", i, v)
end
for i, v in ipairs({ 1, 2, nil, 4 }) do
	print("ipairs", i, v)
end

for i = 1, 2, 0.5 do
	print("float", i)
end
for i = 3, 1, -1 do
	print("down", i)
end
for i = 1, 0 do
	print("never", i)
end
for i = 1.0, 3 do
	print("float start", i)
end

local calls = 0
local function bound(v)
	calls += 1
	return v
end
for i = bound(1), bound(3), bound(1) do
	print("bounded", i)
end
print("bound calls", calls)

-- writing the loop variable changes only this iteration's copy
for i = 1, 3 do
	local before = i
	i = i * 10
	print("copy", before, i)
end

-- a while loop with two exits and a repeat that runs once
local n, steps = 27, 0
while true do
	if n == 1 then
		break
	end
	if steps > 200 then
		print("too long")
		break
	end
	n = if n % 2 == 0 then n // 2 else 3 * n + 1
	steps += 1
end
print("collatz", steps)
repeat
	steps -= 1
until true
print("after repeat", steps)

-- nested loops where the inner break and continue only touch the inner loop
local found = {}
for i = 1, 4 do
	for j = 1, 4 do
		if j > i then
			break
		end
		if (i + j) % 2 == 1 then
			continue
		end
		found[#found + 1] = i * 10 + j
	end
end
print(table.concat(found, " "))

-- for loops: generic for over custom iterators (stateless, stateful, next directly), numeric for
-- with float and negative steps, bounds evaluated once, and a body that writes its loop variable
local function range(n)
	local i = 0
	return function()
		i += 1
		if i <= n then
			return i, i * i
		end
	end
end
for i, sq in range(3) do
	print("range", i, sq)
end

local function evens(t, i)
	i += 2
	if t[i] ~= nil then
		return i, t[i]
	end
end
local list = { "a", "b", "c", "d", "e" }
for i, v in evens, list, -1 do
	print("evens", i, v)
end

local sorted = { 10, 20, 30 }
for i, v in next, sorted do
	print("next", i, v)
end
for i, v in ipairs({ 1, 2, nil, 4 }) do
	print("ipairs", i, v)
end

for i = 1, 2, 0.5 do
	print("float", i)
end
for i = 3, 1, -1 do
	print("down", i)
end
for i = 1, 0 do
	print("never", i)
end
for i = 1.0, 3 do
	print("float start", i)
end

local calls = 0
local function bound(v)
	calls += 1
	return v
end
for i = bound(1), bound(3), bound(1) do
	print("bounded", i)
end
print("bound calls", calls)

-- writing the loop variable changes only this iteration's copy
for i = 1, 3 do
	local before = i
	i = i * 10
	print("copy", before, i)
end

-- a while loop with two exits and a repeat that runs once
local n, steps = 27, 0
while true do
	if n == 1 then
		break
	end
	if steps > 200 then
		print("too long")
		break
	end
	n = if n % 2 == 0 then n // 2 else 3 * n + 1
	steps += 1
end
print("collatz", steps)
repeat
	steps -= 1
until true
print("after repeat", steps)

-- nested loops where the inner break and continue only touch the inner loop
local found = {}
for i = 1, 4 do
	for j = 1, 4 do
		if j > i then
			break
		end
		if (i + j) % 2 == 1 then
			continue
		end
		found[#found + 1] = i * 10 + j
	end
end
print(table.concat(found, " "))

-- for loops: generic for over custom iterators (stateless, stateful, next directly), numeric for
-- with float and negative steps, bounds evaluated once, and a body that writes its loop variable
local function range(n)
	local i = 0
	return function()
		i += 1
		if i <= n then
			return i, i * i
		end
	end
end
for i, sq in range(3) do
	print("range", i, sq)
end

local function evens(t, i)
	i += 2
	if t[i] ~= nil then
		return i, t[i]
	end
end
local list = { "a", "b", "c", "d", "e" }
for i, v in evens, list, -1 do
	print("evens", i, v)
end

local sorted = { 10, 20, 30 }
for i, v in next, sorted do
	print("next", i, v)
end
for i, v in ipairs({ 1, 2, nil, 4 }) do
	print("ipairs", i, v)
end

for i = 1, 2, 0.5 do
	print("float", i)
end
for i = 3, 1, -1 do
	print("down", i)
end
for i = 1, 0 do
	print("never", i)
end
for i = 1.0, 3 do
	print("float start", i)
end

local calls = 0
local function bound(v)
	calls += 1
	return v
end
for i = bound(1), bound(3), bound(1) do

-- closures made in loops: each iteration of a for loop has its own variable, a while loop's
-- local is fresh each time round, and an upvalue written after capture is shared
local fns = {}
for i = 1, 3 do
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return i
	end
end
local k = 0
while k < 3 do
	k += 1
	local j = k * 10
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return j
	end
end
for _, v in ipairs({ "a", "b" }) do
	local copy = v
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		copy = copy .. "!"
		return copy
	end
end
for idx, f in ipairs(fns) do
	print(idx, f(), f())
end

-- one variable captured by two closures, then changed from outside
local function counter()
	local n = 0
	local function inc()
		n += 1
		return n
	end
	local function get()
		return n
	end
	n = 100
	return inc, get
end
local inc, get = counter()
inc()
print(get(), inc(), get())

-- a loop variable shadowed inside the body, and the outer one read after
local total = 0
for i = 1, 4 do
	local i = i * 2
	total += i
end
local i = "outer"
print(total, i)

-- the loop body's local captured, then the loop exits early
local saved
for n = 1, 10 do
	local sq = n * n
	if sq > 20 then
		saved = function()
			return sq
		end
		break
	end
end
print(saved())

-- repeat whose condition reads a local from the body, captured by a closure there
local seen = {}
local r = 0
repeat
	r += 1
	local stop = r >= 3
	seen[r] = function()
		return stop
	end
until stop
print(r, seen[1](), seen[3]())

-- closures made in loops: each iteration of a for loop has its own variable, a while loop's
-- local is fresh each time round, and an upvalue written after capture is shared
local fns = {}
for i = 1, 3 do
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return i
	end
end
local k = 0
while k < 3 do
	k += 1
	local j = k * 10
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return j
	end
end
for _, v in ipairs({ "a", "b" }) do
	local copy = v
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		copy = copy .. "!"
		return copy
	end
end
for idx, f in ipairs(fns) do
	print(idx, f(), f())
end

-- one variable captured by two closures, then changed from outside
local function counter()
	local n = 0
	local function inc()
		n += 1
		return n
	end
	local function get()
		return n
	end
	n = 100
	return inc, get
end
local inc, get = counter()
inc()
print(get(), inc(), get())

-- a loop variable shadowed inside the body, and the outer one read after
local total = 0
for i = 1, 4 do
	local i = i * 2
	total += i
end
local i = "outer"
print(total, i)

-- the loop body's local captured, then the loop exits early
local saved
for n = 1, 10 do
	local sq = n * n
	if sq > 20 then
		saved = function()
			return sq
		end
		break
	end
end
print(saved())

-- repeat whose condition reads a local from the body, captured by a closure there
local seen = {}
local r = 0
repeat
	r += 1
	local stop = r >= 3
	seen[r] = function()
		return stop
	end
until stop
print(r, seen[1](), seen[3]())

entries.source:
-- closures made in loops: each iteration of a for loop has its own variable, a while loop's
-- local is fresh each time round, and an upvalue written after capture is shared
local fns = {}
for i = 1, 3 do
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return i
	end
end
local k = 0
while k < 3 do
	k += 1
	local j = k * 10
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return j
	end
end
for _, v in ipairs({ "a", "b" }) do
	local copy = v
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		copy = copy .. "!"
		return copy
	end
end
for idx, f in ipairs(fns) do
	print(idx, f(), f())
end

-- one variable captured by two closures, then changed from outside
local function counter()
	local n = 0
	local function inc()
		n += 1
		return n
	end
	local function get()
		return n
	end
	n = 100
	return inc, get
end
local inc, get = counter()
inc()
print(get(), inc(), get())

-- a loop variable shadowed inside the body, and the outer one read after
local total = 0
for i = 1, 4 do
	local i = i * 2
	total += i
end
local i = "outer"
print(total, i)

-- the loop body's local captured, then the loop exits early
local saved
for n = 1, 10 do
	local sq = n * n
	if sq > 20 then
		saved = function()
			return sq
		end
		break
	end
end
print(saved())

-- repeat whose condition reads a local from the body, captured by a closure there
local seen = {}
local r = 0
repeat
	r += 1
	local stop = r >= 3
	seen[r] = function()
		return stop
	end
until stop
print(r, seen[1](), seen[3]())

-- closures made in loops: each iteration of a for loop has its own variable, a while loop's
-- local is fresh each time round, and an upvalue written after capture is shared
local fns = {}
for i = 1, 3 do
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return i
	end
end
local k = 0
while k < 3 do
	k += 1
	local j = k * 10
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return j
	end
end
for _, v in ipairs({ "a", "b" }) do
	local copy = v
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		copy = copy .. "!"
		return copy
	end
end
for idx, f in ipairs(fns) do
	print(idx, f(), f())
end

-- one variable captured by two closures, then changed from outside
local function counter()
	local n = 0
	local function inc()
		n += 1
		return n
	end
	local function get()
		return n
	end
	n = 100
	return inc, get
end
local inc, get = counter()
inc()
print(get(), inc(), get())

-- a loop variable shadowed inside the body, and the outer one read after
local total = 0
for i = 1, 4 do
	local i = i * 2
	total += i
end
local i = "outer"
print(total, i)

-- the loop body's local captured, then the loop exits early
local saved
for n = 1, 10 do
	local sq = n * n
	if sq > 20 then
		saved = function()
			return sq
		end
		break
	end
end
print(saved())

local r = 0
repeat
	r += 1

	seen[r] = function()
		return stop
	end
until stop

-- closures made in loops: each iteration of a for loop has its own variable, a while loop's
-- local is fresh each time round, and an upvalue written after capture is shared
local fns = {}
for i = 1, 3 do
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return i
	end
end
local k = 0
while k < 3 do
	k += 1
	local j = k * 10
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return j
	end
end
for _, v in ipairs({ "a", "b" }) do
	local copy = v
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		copy = copy .. "!"
		return copy
	end
end
for idx, f in ipairs(fns) do
	print(idx, f(), f())
end

-- one variable captured by two closures, then changed from outside
local function counter()
	local n = 0
	local function inc()
		n += 1
		return n
	end
	local function get()
		return n
	end
	n = 100
	return inc, get
end
local inc, get = counter()
inc()
print(get(), inc(), get())

-- a loop variable shadowed inside the body, and the outer one read after
local total = 0
for i = 1, 4 do
	local i = i * 2
	total += i
end
local i = "outer"
print(total, i)

-- the loop body's local captured, then the loop exits early
local saved
for n = 1, 10 do
	local sq = n * n
	if sq > 20 then
		saved = function()
			return sq
		end
		break
	end
end
print(saved())

-- repeat whose condition reads a local from the body, captured by a closure there
local seen = {}
local r = 0
repeat
	r += 1
	local stop = r >= 3
	seen[r] = function()
		return stop
	end
until stop
print(r, seen[1](), seen[3]())

-- loops whose exits carry a value out, and a loop body that needs a goto to structure
do
	local Entry = {get = function() return {[2] = {seen = true}} end}
	local function seen(id)
		local e = Entry.get()[id]
		return e ~= nil and e.seen ~= nil
	end
	local function pick(tips)
		local index = nil
		for i, tip in tips do
			if tip.show and not seen(tip.id) then
				index = i
				break
			end
		end
		if index == nil then
			return false
		end
		local ok, v = pcall(function()
			return tips[index].id * 100
		end)
		return ok, v
	end
	print(pick({{show = false, id = 1}, {show = true, id = 2}, {show = true, id = 3}, {show = true, id = 4}}))
	print(pick({{show = true, id = 2}}))
end
do
	local function nextShown(tips, from)
		local index = nil
		for i = from + 1, #tips do
			if tips[i].toShow then
				index = i
				break
			end
		end
		if index ~= nil then
			return "show " .. index .. " " .. tips[index].id
		end
		return "none"
	end
	local tips = {{toShow = true, id = "a"}, {toShow = false, id = "b"}, {toShow = true, id = "c"}}
	print(nextShown(tips, 0), nextShown(tips, 1), nextShown(tips, 3))
end
do
	local function findKey(t, want)
		local key = nil
		for k, v in t do
			if v == want then
				key = k
				break
			end
		end
		if key ~= nil then
			return "found " .. key
		end
		return "none"
	end
	print(findKey({"x", "y", "z"}, "y"), findKey({"x"}, "q"))
end
do
	local function conv(list)
		local out = {}
		for _, v in list do
			if typeof(v) ~= "number" then
				v = tonumber(v) or -1
			end
			table.insert(out, v * 2)
		end
		return table.concat(out, ",")
	end
	local function conv2(n)
		local out = {}
		for i = 1, n do
			if i % 2 == 0 then
				i = i * 100
			end
			table.insert(out, i)
		end
		return table.concat(out, ",")
	end
	print(conv({1, "2", "x", 4}), conv2(4))
end
do
	local function m(items, opts)
		local res = {}
		for _, it in items do
			if it.name then
				local n = it.name
				if opts and opts.skip and opts.skip[n .. "*"] then
					res[n] = "skip*"
				elseif opts and opts.skip and opts.skip[n] then
					res[n] = "skip"
				else
					local k = it.kind
					if k == 1 then
						res[n] = "one"
					elseif k == 2 then
						res[n] = "two"
					else
						if k ~= 3 then
							continue
						end
						res[n] = "three"
					end
				end
			else
				if it.kind ~= 9 then
					continue
				end
				res.schema = "s"
			end
		end
		local keys = {}
		for k, v in res do table.insert(keys, k .. "=" .. v) end
		table.sort(keys)
		return table.concat(keys, ",")
	end
	local items = {{name = "a", kind = 1}, {name = "b", kind = 2}, {name = "c", kind = 3}, {name = "d", kind = 4}, {kind = 9}, {name = "e", kind = 1}, {name = "f", kind = 1}}
	print(m(items, nil))
	print(m(items, {skip = {["a*"] = true, b = true}}))
	print(m(items, {}))
end

entries.source:
-- loops whose exits carry a value out, and a loop body that needs a goto to structure
do
	local Entry = {get = function() return {[2] = {seen = true}} end}
	local function seen(id)
		local e = Entry.get()[id]
		return e ~= nil and e.seen ~= nil
	end
	local function pick(tips)
		local index = nil
		for i, tip in tips do
			if tip.show and not seen(tip.id) then
				index = i
				break
			end
		end
		if index == nil then
			return false
		end
		local ok, v = pcall(function()
			return tips[index].id * 100
		end)
		return ok, v
	end
	print(pick({{show = false, id = 1}, {show = true, id = 2}, {show = true, id = 3}, {show = true, id = 4}}))
	print(pick({{show = true, id = 2}}))
end
do
	local function nextShown(tips, from)
		local index = nil
		for i = from + 1, #tips do
			if tips[i].toShow then
				index = i
				break
			end
		end
		if index ~= nil then
			return "show " .. index .. " " .. tips[index].id
		end
		return "none"
	end
	local tips = {{toShow = true, id = "a"}, {toShow = false, id = "b"}, {toShow = true, id = "c"}}
	print(nextShown(tips, 0), nextShown(tips, 1), nextShown(tips, 3))
end
do
	local function findKey(t, want)
		local key = nil
		for k, v in t do
			if v == want then
				key = k
				break
			end
		end
		if key ~= nil then
			return "found " .. key
		end
		return "none"
	end
	print(findKey({"x", "y", "z"}, "y"), findKey({"x"}, "q"))
end
do
	local function conv(list)
		local out = {}
		for _, v in list do
			if typeof(v) ~= "number" then
				v = tonumber(v) or -1
			end
			table.insert(out, v * 2)
		end
		return table.concat(out, ",")
	end
	local function conv2(n)
		local out = {}
		for i = 1, n do
			if i % 2 == 0 then
				i = i * 100
			end
			table.insert(out, i)
		end
		return table.concat(out, ",")
	end
	print(conv({1, "2", "x", 4}), conv2(4))
end
do
	local function m(items, opts)
		local res = {}
		for _, it in items do
			if it.name then
				local n = it.name
				if opts and opts.skip and opts.skip[n .. "*"] then
					res[n] = "skip*"
				elseif opts and opts.skip and opts.skip[n] then
					res[n] = "skip"
				else
					local k = it.kind
					if k == 1 then
						res[n] = "one"
					elseif k == 2 then
						res[n] = "two"
					else
						if k ~= 3 then
							continue
						end
						res[n] = "three"
					end
				end
			else
				if it.kind ~= 9 then
					continue
				end
				res.schema = "s"
			end
		end
		local keys = {}
		for k, v in res do table.insert(keys, k .. "=" .. v) end
		table.sort(keys)
		return table.concat(keys, ",")
	end
	local items = {{name = "a", kind = 1}, {name = "b", kind = 2}, {name = "c", kind = 3}, {name = "d", kind = 4}, {kind = 9}, {name = "e", kind = 1}, {name = "f", kind = 1}}
	print(m(items, nil))
	print(m(items, {skip = {["a*"] = true, b = true}}))
	print(m(items, {}))
end

-- loops whose exits carry a value out, and a loop body that needs a goto to structure
do
	local Entry = {get = function() return {[2] = {seen = true}} end}
	local function seen(id)
		local e = Entry.get()[id]
		return e ~= nil and e.seen ~= nil
	end
	local function pick(tips)
		local index = nil
		for i, tip in tips do
			if tip.show and not seen(tip.id) then
				index = i
				break
			end
		end
		if index == nil then
			return false
		end
		local ok, v = pcall(function()
			return tips[index].id * 100
		end)
		return ok, v
	end
	print(pick({{show = false, id = 1}, {show = true, id = 2}, {show = true, id = 3}, {show = true, id = 4}}))
	print(pick({{show = true, id = 2}}))
end
do
	local function nextShown(tips, from)
		local index = nil
		for i = from + 1, #tips do
			if tips[i].toShow then
				index = i
				break
			end
		end
		if index ~= nil then
			return "show " .. index .. " " .. tips[index].id
		end
		return "none"
	end
	local tips = {{toShow = true, id = "a"}, {toShow = false, id = "b"}, {toShow = true, id = "c"}}
	print(nextShown(tips, 0), nextShown(tips, 1), nextShown(tips, 3))
end
do
	local function findKey(t, want)
		local key = nil
		for k, v in t do
			if v == want then
				key = k
				break
			end
		end
		if key ~= nil then
			return "found " .. key
		end
		return "none"
	end
	print(findKey({"x", "y", "z"}, "y"), findKey({"x"}, "q"))
end
do
	local function conv(list)
		local out = {}
		for _, v in list do
			if typeof(v) ~= "number" then
				v = tonumber(v) or -1
			end
			table.insert(out, v * 2)
		end
		return table.concat(out, ",")
	end
	local function conv2(n)
		local out = {}
		for i = 1, n do
			if i % 2 == 0 then
				i = i * 100
			end
			table.insert(out, i)
		end
		return table.concat(out, ",")
	end
	print(conv({1, "2", "x", 4}), conv2(4))
end
do
	local function m(items, opts)
		local res = {}
		for _, it in items do
			if it.name then
				local n = it.name
				if opts and opts.skip and opts.skip[n .. "*"] then
					res[n] = "skip*"
				elseif opts and opts.skip and opts.skip[n] then
					res[n] = "skip"
				else
					local k = it.kind
					if k == 1 then
						res[n] = "one"
					elseif k == 2 then
						res[n] = "two"
					else
						if k ~= 3 then
							continue
						end
						res[n] = "three"
					end
				end
			else
				if it.kind ~= 9 then
					continue
				end
				res.schema = "s"
			end
		end
		local keys = {}
		for k, v in res do table.insert(keys, k .. "=" .. v) end
		table.sort(keys)
		return table.concat(keys, ",")
	end
	local items = {{name = "a", kind = 1}, {name = "b", kind = 2}, {name = "c", kind = 3}, {name = "d", kind = 4}, {kind = 9}, {name = "e", kind = 1}, {name = "f", kind = 1}}
	print(m(items, nil))
	print(m(items, {skip = {["a*"] = true, b = true}}))
	print(m(items, {}))
end

-- breaks, continues and returns out of loops, each checked by running both versions
do
	local function find(t, x)
		local found = nil
		for i, v in t do
			if v == x then
				found = i
				break
			end
		end
		if found == nil then
			return "none"
		end
		return found
	end
	print(find({1, 5, 3, 5}, 5), find({1, 2}, 9), find({}, 1))
end
do
	local function first_even(n)
		local r
		for i = 1, n do
			if i % 2 == 0 and i > 3 then
				r = i
				break
			end
		end
		return r
	end
	print(first_even(10), first_even(3))
end
do
	local function f(a, t)
		local hit = 0
		if a then
			for _, v in t do
				if v > 2 then
					hit = v
					break
				end
			end
		else
			hit = -1
		end
		return hit * 10
	end
	print(f(true, {1, 3, 4}), f(true, {1}), f(false, {9}))
end

-- breaks, continues and returns out of loops, each checked by running both versions
do
	local function find(t, x)
		local found = nil
		for i, v in t do
			if v == x then
				found = i
				break
			end
		end
		if found == nil then
			return "none"
		end
		return found
	end
	print(find({1, 5, 3, 5}, 5), find({1, 2}, 9), find({}, 1))
end
do
	local function first_even(n)
		local r
		for i = 1, n do
			if i % 2 == 0 and i > 3 then
				r = i
				break
			end
		end
		return r
	end
	print(first_even(10), first_even(3))
end
do
	local function f(a, t)
		local hit = 0
		if a then
			for _, v in t do
				if v > 2 then
					hit = v
					break
				end
			end
		else
			hit = -1
		end
		return hit * 10
	end
	print(f(true, {1, 3, 4}), f(true, {1}), f(false, {9}))
end
do
	local out = {}
	for i = 1, 4 do
		for j = 1, 4 do
			if j > i then
				break
			end
			if (i + j) % 2 == 1 then
				continue
			end
			table.insert(out, i * 10 + j)
		end
		if i == 3 then
			continue
		end
		table.insert(out, -i)
	end
	print(table.concat(out, ","))
end
do
	local function g(n)
		local i, s = 0, 0
		while i < n do
			i += 1
			if i % 3 == 0 then
				continue
			end
			if s > 20 then
				break
			end
			s += i
		end
		return i, s
	end
	print(g(5), g(100))
end
do
	local function h(n)
		local i, acc = 0, {}
		repeat
			i += 1
			if i == 2 then
				continue
			end
			table.insert(acc, i)
		until i >= n
		return table.concat(acc, " ")
	end
	print(h(5), h(1))
end
do
	local function any_neg(t)
		for _, row in t do
			for _, v in row do
				if v < 0 then
					return true, v
				end
			end
		end
		return false
	end
	print(any_neg({{1, 2}, {3, -4, -5}}), any_neg({{1}}))
end
do
	local fs = {}
	for i = 1, 3 do
		local j = i * 2
		if i == 2 then
			continue
		end
		table.insert(fs, function() return i + j end)
	end
	local r = {}
	for _, f in fs do table.insert(r, f()) end
	print(table.concat(r, ","))
end
do
	local function f(list, flag)
		local n = 0
		for _, v in list do
			n += 1
			if v > 10 then
				if flag then
					print("big flag", v)
					return n
				else
					print("big", v)
					return -n
				end
			end
		end
		return 0
	end
	local function g(list)
		for _, v in list do
			if v == 1 then
				print("one")
				return
			elseif v == 2 then
				print("two")
				return
			end
			print("other", v)
		end
		print("end")
	end
	print(f({1, 2, 30, 40}, true), f({1, 50}, false), f({1}, true))
	g({5, 2, 1}) g({5, 6})
end
